steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Spray a 9-inch pie pan with non-stick cooking spray.

Spread cream cheese on the bottom of the pie pan. Pour pizza sauce over the cream cheese, and spread it so that there is an even layer of sauce. Sprinkle with pepperoni, onion, and olives. Top with mozzarella cheese.
Bake at 400 degrees F (200 degrees C) for 20 to 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pizza Dip
raw_recipe.description: Great dip for parties or for snacks for the family. Easy to prepare. Serve with pita bread chips, crackers, or even a thin sliced baguette.
raw_recipe.name: Pizza Dip

review.reviewBody: I don't like tweeking recipes but I did on this one and it turn out really good. I added italian seasoning, garlic powder, and about 3 ozs of sour cream to the cream cheese and mixed it and followed the recipe to the "T" for the rest of it. Excellent!!! Will make again but I will double.

I used reduced fat cream cheese, homemade marinara sauce I'd defrosted from my freezer (The Best Marinara Sauce, which is also from this site), I doubled the pepperoni and I used Tillamook's italian cheese blend. This was a quick dip I could mix up and throw in my mini-crockpot before our morning errands and have it be done right as my boys were getting hungry. They loved having dip-able pizza and I liked it because it used on hand pantry ingredients. I served it with day old baguettes I bought at Fred Meyer from the discount rack for super cheap.

Used homemade pizza sauce. This was very good for using a little of this and that for a late snack. Just right size for using toaster oven and not the big oven. Great with tortilla chips. Plan to use toasted baguette bread next time. Hubby suggested Italian sausage next time since is a big fan of it.

After reading other reviews, I was torn between whether to mix the cream cheese and pizza sauce in a blender or layer. At first I decided to follow the recipe exactly, but I was afraid that people would bite into nothing but pizza sauce. I removed the combo and placed in a blender and got a pretty tasty sauce. I added the ingredients on top. The biggest recommendation that I have is to not completely cover with mozzarella cheese...just lighly sprinkle instead. This is because once the cheese cooled, it formed a hard layer on top that was hard to dip. As much as i love cheese it's best to keep it spread out where it doesn't clump together. I baked garlic bread and sliced into cubes for dipping, which was really tasty.

It comes out better if you put pepperoni slices ON TOP of the cheese so the cheese doesn't get brown & crusty. Add in other toppings as you like them on top of the sauce.....sausage, mushrooms, peppers, etc. I serve with Fritos Scoops - they hold up well to the cheese. ALWAYS a hit at parties!

To Stir or Not to Stir: I've made this twice now. The first time I did not stir the pizza sauce and cream cheese and I loved it. Boyfriend liked it until the last bite when he got a glob of cream cheese without much sauce. He thinks he doesn't like cream cheese, so if he can identify it, then he says yuck (he has zero idea of how much cream cheese he eats). The second time I mixed a little of the pizza sauce into the cream cheese. While I liked it slightly better NOT mixed together, he LOVED it the second time. He had no idea it contained cream cheese or that it was the same dip as the first time. Each time I used homemade pizza sauce and added cheddar and parmesan that I had hanging around.

I went with the basics of this recipe and modified it slightly according to reviews and my own preferences. I added italian seasonings, oregano, and fennel seed to the cream cheese; used 1/2 can of sauce and 1/2 can drained diced italian tomatos, and no olives. It was a hit! Everyone liked the soft baguette bread better than the crunchier/toasted bagettes. Either way, I have no dip or bread left!

I made this for years! Always a hit!! I buy pizza crust, then brush it with butter. Then I add Parmesian cheese & garlic powder. Bake at 400 degrees aprox. 10 minutes. Cut into bite size strips & dip away!! I always double this recipe for a party,etc.

I tweaked this recipe a bit. I added some Italian seasoning, garlic powder, a little bit of onion powder, a couple shakes of the Crushed Red Pepper Flakes and about 3 1/2 tbl of sour cream to the cream cheese. Came out amazing. Thank you for sharing

This dip is so good! I mixed in about 1 cup of sour cream with the pizza sauce, and then I added finely chopped green pepper, mushrooms and black olives. I also sprinkled on some Mrs. Dash extra spicy seasoning and it gave it extra flavor. I didn't add the pepperoni or the onion, but I think next time I'll try it with some onion.

Excellent recipe..been making it for a long time. I like to add sour cream to the cream cheese mixture, 1 tsp of oregano and 1/2 tsp of cayenne pepper, which gives it a little kick. Great with chips and toasted baguette slices.
i love it
It turned out pretty good! It's just your basic pizza dip. Next time I'd go about 6oz of cream cheese and add some Italian seasoning to flavor I

This was a decent base recipe. First and foremost as some reviewers have said, the cheese will solidify and so I highly suggest mixing it in and then sprinkling grated Parmesan cheese over it all. This also needs salt and some seasonings.

Brought it to a dinner party, the dip was called "lasagna over toast" it was a total hit. I saw another similar, more complicated recipe, and decided to do this one instead; I was definitely not sorry, the dish was cleaned. I did the recipe exactly as stated except I mixed the cream cheese and pizza sauce.
pretty bland even though I used red pepper flakes. Don't like how the cream cheese looks when melted and shredded cheese became a big blob.
Very good-everyone loved it! I served with pieces of garlic bread and crackers!
I made this dip for my hometeam at church. I combined all the ingredients in my small slow cooker and it turned out perfect on low. Everyone loved it!!!

This appetizer was great and really easy to make! I modified it a bit by adding Italian seasoning, green pepper, provolone and parmesan cheeses. I didn't use any onion or olives. I will definitely make this again.

This was great! I needed a dip recipe in a pinch, and this was super easy to put together. Our guests don't eat pork, so I used turkey sausage instead, and it tasted just fine. We also skipped the olives, but I think it would be yummy with them as well. I did add garlic powder and Italian seasoning to the cream cheese as others suggested, and I think it helped give the dip a little more flavor. Will definitely make again!
